nodes.summary: Uniqueness of the steady state (Goldbeter–Koshland 1981, Eq. 7). For `K₁, K₂ > 0`, if `0 < W < 1` and `rateRatio K₁ K₂ W = v` with `v > 0`, then `W` is the Goldbeter–Koshland function.
nodes.title: Uniqueness of the steady state

nodes.summary: For `v, K₁, K₂ > 0` the Goldbeter–Koshland function lies in `(0, 1)`.
nodes.title: Goldbeter–Koshland function lies strictly between 0 and 1

nodes.summary: Equal maximal rates (Goldbeter–Koshland 1981, Eq. 9): for `V₁ = V₂` and `K₁, K₂ > 0` the steady-state modified fraction is `K₂ / (K₁ + K₂)`.
nodes.title: Equal maximal rates

nodes.summary: The Goldbeter–Koshland function: the steady-state mole fraction of modified protein when `V₁ / V₂ = v` (Goldbeter–Koshland 1981, Eq. 7, rationalized so that it also covers `v = 1`, Eq. 9). Meaningful for `v, K₁, K₂ > 0`.
nodes.title: Goldbeter–Koshland function

nodes.summary: Hill response coefficient (Goldbeter–Koshland 1981, Eq. 11). For a Hill response with `n > 0` and `K > 0`, if `S₉, S₁ > 0` give 90% and 10% response, then `S₉ / S₁ = 81 ^ (1 / n)`.
nodes.title: Hill response coefficient

nodes.summary: The fraction of a Hill response `Sⁿ / (Kⁿ + Sⁿ)` with half-saturation constant `K` and Hill coefficient `n` (meaningful for `S, K > 0`, `n > 0`).
nodes.title: Hill response function

nodes.summary: Michaelis–Menten response (`n = 1`): going from 10% to 90% of the response takes an 81-fold increase of the stimulus.
nodes.title: Michaelis–Menten response

nodes.summary: For `K₁, K₂ > 0` the response coefficient exceeds `1`: the switch is never infinitely sharp.
nodes.title: Response coefficient exceeds 1

nodes.summary: The Goldbeter–Koshland function is a steady state (Goldbeter–Koshland 1981, Eq. 7): for `v, K₁, K₂ > 0`, `rateRatio K₁ K₂ (goldbeterKoshland v K₁ K₂) = v`.
nodes.title: The Goldbeter–Koshland function is a steady state

nodes.summary: The value of `V₁ / V₂` for which the mole fraction `W` of modified protein is at steady state (Goldbeter–Koshland 1981, Eq. 8): `W (1 - W + K₁) / ((1 - W) (W + K₂))`. Meaningful for `0 < W < 1` and `K₁, K₂ > 0`; at `W = 1` Lean's `a / 0 = 0` gives the junk value `0`.
nodes.title: Rate ratio at a given steady-state modified fraction

nodes.summary: The response coefficient (Goldbeter–Koshland 1981, Eq. 10): for `K₁, K₂ > -0.1`, `R_v = 81 (K₁ + 0.1)(K₂ + 0.1) / ((K₁ + 0.9)(K₂ + 0.9))`.
nodes.title: The response coefficient

nodes.summary: For `K₁, K₂ > 0` the response coefficient is below the Michaelis–Menten value `81`.
nodes.title: Response coefficient is below the Michaelis–Menten value 81

nodes.summary: The response coefficient `R_v`: the ratio of the values of `V₁ / V₂` giving 90% and 10% modified protein at steady state (Goldbeter–Koshland 1981).
nodes.title: Response coefficient of a covalent modification cycle

nodes.summary: Steady state of the modification cycle (Goldbeter–Koshland 1981, Eq. 8). For `V₂ > 0`, `K₁, K₂ > 0` and `0 < W < 1`, modification and demodification balance, `V₁ (1 - W) / (K₁ + 1 - W) = V₂ W / (K₂ + W)`, iff `V₁ / V₂ = rateRatio K₁ K₂ W`.
nodes.title: Steady state of the modification cycle

nodes.summary: `rateRatio K₁ K₂` is strictly increasing on `(0, 1)` for `K₁, K₂ > 0`: it is the product of the positive increasing functions `W / (W + K₂)` and `1 + K₁ / (1 - W)`.
nodes.title: Rate ratio is strictly increasing in the modified fraction

nodes.summary: As both `K₁, K₂ → ∞` the response coefficient tends to `81`, the value of a Michaelis–Menten response.
nodes.title: First-order limit

nodes.summary: As both `K₁, K₂ → 0` the response coefficient tends to `1`.
nodes.title: Zero-order ultrasensitivity

can_prove.label: ready to prove
can_prove.meaning: Statement is in Lean and nothing it needs is blocked, so the proof can start.

can_state.label: ready to state
can_state.meaning: Everything its statement uses is in Lean, so the statement can be written in Lean.

conditional.label: conditionally proved
conditional.meaning: Proof compiles, but rests on an open statement without a recorded Lean proof.

fully_proved.label: fully proved
fully_proved.meaning: Proved, and every prerequisite is fully proved too.

inventory_checked.label: inventory checked
inventory_checked.meaning: Module inventory checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

inventory_pending.label: inventory pending
inventory_pending.meaning: Module inventory not yet checked in full; it records inspection, not a mathematical proof.

not_ready.label: not ready
not_ready.meaning: Needs more blueprint work before it can be attempted.

proved.label: proved
proved.meaning: Proof compiles, but something it rests on is not finished.

stated.label: statement formalized
stated.meaning: Statement is in Lean; the proof is not.
